current_example.problem:
Find $\displaystyle\lim_{x\rightarrow 0^-} f(x)$ and $\displaystyle\lim_{x\rightarrow 0^+} f(x)$ for the function given below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14218806/assets/1dc9fd5dc473e15939a50fbb209475d580be540fb8c9a2bc8602a6a9724b08bd.png)
current_example.worked_solution:
As $x$ approaches $0$ from the *left*, the function $f(x)$ approaches $1.$ Therefore,

$$
\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,0^{-}}f(x) = 1 \, .
$$

Likewise, as $x$ approaches $0$ from the *right*, the function $f(x)$ approaches $1.$ Therefore,

$$
\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,0^{+}}f(x) = 1 \, .
$$

In conclusion, we have

$$
\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,0^{-}}f(x)=\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,0^{+}}f(x)=1 \,.
$$
